column1: # Corrections to the Hebrew speaker layer (shoresh/macula/build_speaker_layer.py applies them last).
# One row per change, keyed on a quotation's first word (MACULA key, 12 digits, as in quotations.tsv `first`).
# field: speaker | first | last | drop | frame | sender_last   (drop: the quotation is not a quotation, value empty; frame: the frame of
#   the chapter that starts with this word, empty for none; sender_last: keyed on a relayed message's formula, the last word of the
#   sender's words, after which the messenger speaks in his own name)
# value: the new speaker name, or the new first / last word key
# reason: how the Hebrew text settles it (required)

column4: Ps 1 has no title and no speaker or addressee of its own: a teaching about the two ways ("אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ"), in the third person throughout
Ps 2 has no title and no single speaker from its start: it quotes the nations (2:3), God (2:6) and the king (2:7-9) and then turns to the kings (2:10-12)

Josh 24:14-15 is Joshua's own appeal: "וְעַתָּה יְראוּ אֶת־יְהוָה" turns to the people with an imperative and speaks of the LORD in the third person, after God's first-person history of 24:2-13 ("וָאֶקַּח", "וָאֶתֵּן")

Ezra 8 is a first-person account of the journey ("וָאֶקְבְּצֵם", "וַנַּחֲנֶה", "וָאָבִינָה"), told as narrative, not speech from its start; the frame stays on Ezra 9, where the account leads into Ezra's prayer
Neh 1 is a first-person account told as narrative ("וָאֶשְׁאָלֵם", "וָאֵשְׁבָה"); Nehemiah's prayer in it (1:5-11) is a quotation of its own
Neh 2 is a first-person account told as narrative ("וָאֶשָּׂא", "וָאָבוֹא", "וָאָקוּם"), with the speeches in it quoted

Dan 4 is Nebuchadnezzar's letter, opened in 3:31 ("נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר מַלְכָּא לְכָל־עַמְמַיָּא … שְׁלָמְכוֹן יִשְׂגֵּא") and told in his own voice from 4:1 ("אֲנָה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר שְׁלֵה הֲוֵית בְּבֵיתִי") to its doxology (4:34)
Dan 8 is Daniel's own account of his vision ("חָזוֹן נִרְאָה אֵלַי אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל", 8:1; "וַאֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל נִהְיֵיתִי", 8:27)
Dan 9 is Daniel's own account ("אֲנִי דָּנִיֵּאל בִּינֹתִי בַּסְּפָרִים", 9:2), in which his prayer (9:4-19) and Gabriel's words (9:22-27) are quoted
Dan 10 is Daniel's own account ("בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל הָיִיתִי מִתְאַבֵּל", 10:2) of the vision that runs to 12:13
